$comment: The template <-> generated-app boundary, written down. Consumed by
scripts/drift-report.sh and by the shared-path step in .claude/commands/wrap.md.
Everything listed under `paths` is meant to stay the same across the template and
the apps generated from it. Everything NOT listed (app/, src/store/, src/theme/,
assets/, store-listing/, IDEA.md, ...) is meant to diverge. That distinction was
previously written down nowhere, which is half of why #145 kept happening.
Pattern semantics: matched with bash `[[ path == glob ]]`, where `*` DOES match a
slash. So `scripts/*` covers everything under scripts/ at any depth, and there is
no need for `**`. Patterns are matched against repo-relative paths.
`mode` is the important field:
identical - must match byte-for-byte after placeholder normalisation. Any
difference is drift and gets reported with a diff.
advisory  - shared in SHAPE but legitimately carries app-specific prose, so
diffing the content is noise. Compared by commit subject instead:
the report lists commits touching the path that one side has and
the other does not. tick's .maestro flows differ from ours by 59
lines, 58 of which are correct app-specific comments and one of
which was an unpropagated fix - content diffing cannot tell those
apart, and commit subjects can.

paths.$comment: Edited alongside eslint.config.js below for the same reason: excluding the gitignored drift clone cache at .claude/scratch/drift/ from test/lint walks.

The two template-*-smoke-test workflows exercise the template AS A TEMPLATE (init.sh, add-backend.sh against a scratch checkout). A generated app's stale copy is not drift - it is a file that stopped applying the moment the app was bootstrapped.
init.sh rewrites the placeholders and then deletes itself from relevance; it differs from tick by 99 lines, all of them correct.

$comment: templates/licenses/{private,public}.txt are init.sh's data files, and init.sh
is already excluded from scripts/* just above. Excluding a consumer while
still shipping its inputs is incoherent: a generated app never re-runs init.sh,
so it never receives the one thing that reads these, and they would sit there
inert forever. The alternative — copying them down so the report goes quiet —
buys silence with two dead files in every app, permanently. Decided rather
than deferred; do not re-open it without a consumer that runs inside an app.
The LICENSE those files install still travels: it is a real file at the app
root, just not one compared here (it is intentionally per-repo, see #155).

paths.$comment: Apps receive this file too (their own /wrap step 2 reads it), so paths changes should be flagged as travel-worthy. But the apps array is inherently per-repo and would always show as drift under a byte diff, which is why advisory (compared by commit subject) rather than identical.

$limitedScopeComment: What a non-descendant repo is compared on. Deliberately tiny: these four are the only parts of the shared surface that mean anything to a repo on a different stack. Comparing a Capacitor app against .claude/skills/rn-* or .github/workflows/eas-preview.yml produces pages of output and zero decisions.

$comment: Advisory-mode triage, 2026-08-24. The advisory set is compared by commit subject, so
it never empties: tick adopts template work in squashed `chore: sync template x.y.z`
commits, and every subject on either side of that squash reads as one-sided forever.
A non-empty history section is therefore the resting state, not a backlog. What follows
is the read that resolved it, so the next run can skim rather than re-derive.
Content-identical despite the diverged subjects — pure squash noise, nothing to do:
src/__tests__/e2e-contract.test.ts, docs/backends/firebase.md, docs/backends/supabase.md.
.maestro/full-journey.yaml, .maestro/persistence.yaml — differ in prose only, and both
copies are correct where they sit. The template says 'the home screen', 'a real app
generated from this template', 'scripts/add-paywall.sh'; tick says 'the clock screen',
'on Tick', 'RevenueCat (#6)'. This is the 58-of-59 case the advisory mode exists for.
Every behavioural fix has already travelled: 180s cold-start waits (tick#14),
centerElement on the Danger Zone scroll, the 700ms swipe and the CTA wait before it.
docs/testing.md — the one path that carried real drift, now resolved both ways.
Upstream in template #158: the check-4 'match the tap, not the id' prose and its
escape-hatch row (tick#17 fixed the code here, and the code travelled, but its
documentation did not), plus a stale '60-second' where the flows now wait 180.
Downstream in tick #22: the drift-report section, which documents scripts/drift-report.sh
as tick PR #21 delivers it.
Staying in tick: the port-8081 / JAVA_HOME block. It is machine narrative ('the Mac Tick
is developed on', '8082 belongs to MealCart'), and its general half is already upstream —
the invisible-port-holder note in the same section, and scripts/e2e.sh's own JAVA_HOME
failure message.
.claude/CLAUDE.md — the cross-repo-propagation section goes downstream in tick #22, for
the same reason as the docs one. The rest stays: init.sh's 18-label set and the LICENSE
visibility switch describe a script a generated app never re-runs, and tick already has
the /wrap Stop hook under a different commit subject.

apps.$comment: MealCart was bootstrapped before most of this existed and has never adopted it. Each entry here is a triaged 'known absent, not a missed fix' - without them the first report is a wall of ABSENT and the second one gets ignored. Re-triage by deleting a line and re-running.
Capacitor + Vite, not Expo. Only the stack-agnostic slice is comparable.
Expo, but predates the current layout (components/, lib/, store/ at the root, no src/).
